Listen to this article Share The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) has ruled out a national grid collapse following the tripping of multiple transmission lines on Friday, which triggered significant load losses in parts of the country. Advertisement Advertisement The operator said the disturbance, which affected electricity supply in parts of the country, resulted from the tripping of transmission lines and did not constitute a system-wide collapse. In a note on its social media platform X on Friday, NISO noted that the Omotosho-Ikeja West transmission line tripped at 12:34pm, causing a significant load drop within the Lagos electricity complex. Read also: NISO restores power system after partial grid disturbance Similarly, at 12:50pm, the Ihovbor-Oshogbo transmission line also tripped alongside the Benin-Egbin and Ihovbor-Ajaokuta transmission lines, resulting in further load losses across some parts of the country. “Following the incidents, prompt emergency response measures were activated by the relevant operational teams in coordination with TCN to stabilise the grid and restore affected transmission lines,” the operator said in the note. Advertisement “NISO confirms that all the affected lines have since been successfully restored to normal operation as of 2:49pm today,” it added. The incidents prompted emergency response measures by operational teams in collaboration with the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) to stabilise the grid and restore the affected transmission lines. Advertisement The clarification comes amid growing questions from Nigerians about the capacity and reliability of the national grid to generate and distribute electricity, particularly as repeated grid disturbances continue to raise concerns about the stability of the country’s power infrastructure. As of 2:46pm on Friday, total load on the national grid stood at 948.00 megawatts against an average of over 3,000MW, highlighting the extent of the disruption around the time the operator was working to restore normal operations. Advertisement Advertisement Ikeja Electric had a load of 133MW, Eko Disco had 132MW, Ibadan Disco had 119MW, and Abuja Disco had 109MW — reflecting significant load shedding across all the DisCos. However, the operator maintained that the incident was a transmission line disturbance rather than a system-wide collapse. Read also: Prof. Abel Olorunnisola: Taking Bells University to the heights of technology “There was no grid collapse,” it clarified in a note. NISO said it remains committed to maintaining grid stability, coordinating system operations and ensuring the reliable and secure operation of the Nigerian electricity grid. The operator urged electricity consumers and the general public to rely on its official communications for accurate information about developments within the national grid.
